questions.text: When you read a book, which direction do your eyes move across a line of words?
questions.explanation: We read English from left to right, and we start at the top of the page and move to the bottom.

questions.text: How many syllables are in the word 'rabbit'? Clap it out: rab-bit.
questions.explanation: The word 'rabbit' has two syllables: 'rab' and 'bit.'

questions.text: What is the FIRST sound you hear in the word 'map'?
questions.explanation: The first sound in 'map' is /m/, the sound the letter M makes.

questions.text: What is the LAST sound you hear in the word 'sit'?
questions.explanation: The last sound in 'sit' is /t/, the sound the letter T makes.

questions.text: Which word starts with the /b/ sound?
questions.explanation: 'Ball' starts with the /b/ sound, which is the sound the letter B makes.

questions.text: The word 'cake' has a long A sound. Which of these words also has a long A sound?
questions.explanation: 'Rain' has the long A sound, just like 'cake.' The letters 'ai' together make the long A sound.

questions.passage: The dog ran to the park. She played with a red ball.
questions.text: What did the dog play with?
questions.explanation: The story says the dog played with a red ball.

questions.passage: Mia and her cat, Fluffy, sat on the porch. Mia read a book while Fluffy took a nap.
questions.text: Who are the characters in this story?
questions.explanation: The two characters in the story are Mia and her cat, Fluffy.

questions.passage: A little bird wanted to fly. Every day she flapped her wings. One morning she jumped from the branch and flew all the way across the yard.
questions.text: What happens at the end of the story?
options: The bird falls to the ground.
The bird flies across the yard.
questions.explanation: At the end of the story, the little bird finally flies all the way across the yard after practicing every day.

questions.passage: This book was written by Jane Park. The pictures were drawn by Tom Hill.
questions.text: Who drew the pictures in this book?
questions.explanation: Tom Hill is the illustrator. The illustrator is the person who draws the pictures.

questions.passage: Frogs live near water. They can jump very far with their strong back legs.
questions.explanation: The text says frogs use their strong back legs to jump very far.

questions.passage: Dogs make good pets. They are friendly and they love to play. Dogs also protect their families.
questions.text: What is this passage mostly about?
questions.explanation: The passage tells three reasons dogs make good pets: they are friendly, they love to play, and they protect families.

questions.text: Which sentence uses a naming word (noun) for a person?
questions.explanation: The word 'teacher' names a person, which makes it a noun. Nouns are words that name a person, place, or thing.

questions.text: Which sentence starts the right way?
questions.explanation: Every sentence must start with a capital letter. 'My cat is soft.' begins with a capital M, so it is correct.

questions.text: Which group of words all belong in the 'animals' category?
questions.explanation: 'Bird, fish, and bear' are all animals. The other choices each include objects that are not animals.
